subject: Microbiology
vignette: A 6-year-old boy in a rural village presents with 3 days of dry cough and wheezing, followed by crampy abdominal discomfort. His mother reports that he passed a large, pale, cylindrical worm in his stool yesterday. A chest radiograph obtained during the cough illness shows patchy migratory infiltrates, and a complete blood count shows eosinophilia. He has been playing in a sandbox and has eaten dirt.
question: Which of the following best describes the route by which this organism infects humans?

options.text: A female mosquito bite that deposits infective larvae
Ingestion of eggs in food contaminated with soil
Ingestion of larvae encysted in striated muscle
Cercariae from a snail intermediate host penetrating skin
Larvae in soil that penetrate intact skin

explanation_correct: Ascaris lumbricoides is the giant roundworm, transmitted by the fecal-oral route through ingestion of eggs from contaminated soil, and it belongs to the ingested group in the First Aid EATTT mnemonic. The eggs are knobby-coated and oval. In heavier infection, larvae migrate through the lungs to the alveoli and produce Loeffler syndrome with pulmonary eosinophilia and cough, which explains this child's chest findings. Other complications include obstruction at the ileocecal valve, biliary obstruction, and intestinal perforation.

explanation_incorrect.A: A female mosquito bite transmits the filarial worms Wuchereria bancrofti and Brugia malayi, which cause lymphatic filariasis and lymphedema rather than stool-passed worms.
explanation_incorrect.C: Larvae encysted in striated muscle are the transmission form of Trichinella spiralis from undercooked pork, causing myalgias and periorbital edema rather than intestinal worms with eosinophilic pneumonia.
explanation_incorrect.D: Cercariae from a snail intermediate host penetrate skin in Schistosoma infection, which produces portal hypertension or bladder carcinoma instead of a large intestinal roundworm.
explanation_incorrect.E: Larvae in soil that penetrate intact skin are the route for Strongyloides stercoralis and the hookworms Ancylostoma and Necator, the group First Aid groups under the SANd mnemonic.

educationalObjective: Ascaris egg ingestion from contaminated soil causes intestinal roundworms, and larval migration to the alveoli produces Loeffler syndrome with pulmonary eosinophilia.

subject: Microbiology
vignette: A 9-year-old boy in a rural village in sub-Saharan Africa presents with fatigue, pica, and poor school performance. He walks barefoot on sandy soil around his home and near a beach. Examination shows pale conjunctivae and tachycardia. Laboratory studies show hemoglobin 7.9 g/dL, mean corpuscular volume 68 fL, a low ferritin level, and elevated platelets. Stool microscopy shows ova consistent with a blood-feeding intestinal worm, and stool occult blood is positive.
question: Which of the following is the most likely consequence of this child's infection?

options.text: Microcytic anemia from chronic intestinal blood loss
Lower extremity elephantiasis with a female mosquito bite history
A pruritic serpiginous rash on the foot
Rectal prolapse following chronic loose stools
Myalgias with periorbital edema after eating pork

explanation_correct: Hookworms such as Ancylostoma species and Necator americanus enter through the skin when larvae penetrate a bare foot walking on contaminated beach or soil. The adult worms attach to the intestinal wall and suck blood, causing chronic microcytic iron deficiency anemia, which is what this child has. First Aid lists iron deficiency anemia as the hint association for Ancylostoma and Necator, and treatment is albendazole or pyrantel pamoate.

explanation_incorrect.C: A pruritic serpiginous rash is cutaneous larva migrans, which is also caused by hookworm larvae, but it is a self-limited skin phase rather than the cause of severe anemia and pica.
explanation_incorrect.D: Rectal prolapse with chronic loose stools is the classic complication of heavy Trichuris trichiura infection, a whipworm that does not suck blood from the intestinal wall.
explanation_incorrect.E: Myalgias with periorbital edema after eating undercooked pork indicate trichinosis from Trichinella spiralis, whose larvae encyst in muscle and do not cause chronic iron deficiency.
explanation_incorrect.B: Elephantiasis with a mosquito bite history is lymphatic filariasis from Wuchereria bancrofti or Brugia malayi, which obstructs lymphatics rather than causing anemia.

educationalObjective: Hookworm larvae that penetrate bare feet become blood-sucking intestinal worms, so the classic consequence is microcytic iron deficiency anemia.

subject: Microbiology
vignette: A 55-year-old man with chronic obstructive pulmonary disease is admitted with an exacerbation and started on high-dose prednisone. One week later he develops fever, dry cough with blood-streaked sputum, diffuse abdominal pain, and a rapidly spreading petechial rash on the abdomen and thighs. He worked on farms in Southeast Asia 30 years ago. Laboratory studies show eosinophilia and gram-negative bacteremia, and stool microscopy shows small, slender larvae rather than eggs.
question: Which of the following organisms most likely explains this presentation?

options.text: Ancylostoma species
Enterobius vermicularis
Trichuris trichiura
Ascaris lumbricoides
Strongyloides stercoralis

explanation_correct: Strongyloides stercoralis enters through the skin when larvae in soil penetrate it, and alone among these nematodes it can complete its life cycle inside the host, so autoinfection can persist for decades after the initial exposure. When cellular immunity declines, especially with corticosteroids or HTLV-1 infection, accelerated autoinfection causes hyperinfection syndrome with gastrointestinal, pulmonary, and cutaneous symptoms, and gut bacteria can be carried into the bloodstream. Diagnosis is by rhabditiform larvae in the stool, and treatment is ivermectin.

explanation_incorrect.A: Ancylostoma hookworms share the skin-penetration route but produce chronic iron deficiency anemia from blood feeding and do not establish host-internal replication.
explanation_incorrect.B: Enterobius vermicularis causes nocturnal perianal pruritus in children, is diagnosed by the tape test for eggs, and does not cause hyperinfection or bacteremia.
explanation_incorrect.C: Trichuris trichiura is ingested as eggs and causes loose stools, anemia, and rectal prolapse in children, with eggs rather than larvae seen in stool.
explanation_incorrect.D: Ascaris also migrates through the lungs and causes eosinophilia, but it cannot replicate within the host, so corticosteroids cannot trigger an autoinfection-driven hyperinfection syndrome.

educationalObjective: Before starting corticosteroids, consider Strongyloides stercoralis, because accelerated autoinfection causes hyperinfection syndrome with bacterial dissemination and requires ivermectin.

subject: Microbiology
vignette: A 47-year-old man who lived in rural Cambodia as a child presents with 3 months of intermittent sharp epigastric pain with nausea, a dry cough, and a pruritic rash over the buttocks and lower back. He reports frequent loose stools and has had multiple courses of antibiotics without improvement. Laboratory studies show eosinophilia, and stool microscopy shows rhabditiform larvae.
question: Which of the following best characterizes this organism's clinical spectrum?

options.text: Rectal prolapse with chronic loose stools in a child
Symptoms of duodenitis, cough, and pruritic skin rash in one patient
Microcytic anemia with a serpiginous rash on the foot
Subcutaneous nodules with loss of visual acuity
Myalgias, periorbital edema, and fever after undercooked pork

explanation_correct: Strongyloides stercoralis is the threadworm, and First Aid emphasizes that it can produce gastrointestinal symptoms such as duodenitis, pulmonary symptoms such as dry cough and hemoptysis, and cutaneous symptoms such as pruritus. This multiorgan spectrum occurs because larvae penetrate the skin, migrate through the lungs, and mature in the small bowel, and in immunosuppression accelerated autoinfection produces hyperinfection syndrome. Larvae in soil penetrate the skin, and rhabditiform larvae are seen in the stool.

explanation_incorrect.A: Rectal prolapse with chronic loose stools in a child is the classic Trichuris trichiura picture, a whipworm acquired by ingesting eggs and diagnosed by eggs in stool rather than larvae.
explanation_incorrect.C: Microcytic anemia with a serpiginous rash describes hookworm infection, which shares the skin entry route but produces blood-loss anemia and does not cause this combined duodenitis-pulmonary-cutaneous picture.
explanation_incorrect.D: Subcutaneous nodules with loss of visual acuity describe Onchocerca volvulus and river blindness, transmitted by the black fly rather than by soil larvae.
explanation_incorrect.E: Myalgias with periorbital edema and fever after undercooked pork describe trichinosis from Trichinella spiralis, whose larvae encyst in striated muscle.

educationalObjective: Strongyloides stercoralis can simultaneously cause duodenitis, cough, and pruritic skin disease because it migrates from skin to lungs to bowel, and it is treated with ivermectin.

subject: Microbiology
vignette: A 10-year-old girl in Brazil is found to have Ascaris lumbricoides eggs on a school screening stool examination. Her neighborhood also has a high rate of hookworm infection in children, and an outreach team is treating soil-transmitted helminths in the community while a local patient is being treated for Onchocerca volvulus river blindness.
question: Which of the following best summarizes the First Aid anthelmintic associations for these organisms?

options.text: Praziquantel as the treatment for all three organisms
Ivermectin as the first-line agent for Ascaris and Trichuris
Metronidazole as the treatment for Strongyloides and hookworm
albendazole, with ivermectin as the first-line agent for Strongyloides
Pyrantel pamoate as the first-line agent for Ascaris and hookworm

explanation_correct: First Aid lists albendazole as the treatment for Ascaris lumbricoides and Trichuris trichiura, with pyrantel pamoate added as an alternative for Enterobius and hookworm. Strongyloides stercoralis is treated with ivermectin or albendazole, and ivermectin is also the drug for Onchocerca volvulus river blindness. The high-yield distinction is between the albendazole-first intestinal nematodes and the ivermectin-first tissue and filarial worms.

explanation_incorrect.A: Praziquantel treats trematodes and cestodes such as Schistosoma, Clonorchis, Taenia, and Diphyllobothrium, and it has no activity against nematodes.
explanation_incorrect.B: Ivermectin is the first-line agent for Strongyloides and Onchocerca rather than for Ascaris and Trichuris, which are albendazole-first in First Aid.
explanation_incorrect.C: Metronidazole is a protozoal drug for Giardia, Entamoeba, and Trichomonas, and it has no anthelmintic activity.
explanation_incorrect.E: Pyrantel pamoate appears as an alternative for Enterobius and hookworm, but First Aid lists albendazole for Ascaris, so this reverses the emphasis.

educationalObjective: albendazole are the standard anthelmintic for Ascaris and Trichuris, while ivermectin is first-line for Strongyloides and Onchocerca volvulus.
